title: Ops guardrails: experimentation playlist + decision heuristic (90d)
content:
Context:
We need a compact, executable playbook that productizes how we run short-burst reliability experiments aimed at maturing guardrails (automated fallbacks, throttles, and SLO-aware routing). This doc is intentionally tactical: a prioritized 90-day experimentation playlist plus the decision heuristic teams should use to graduate an experiment into a policy or roll it back.

Why this now:
- Dedicated and private customers have started calling out inconsistent tail latency under mixed workloads.
- Recent on-call incidents show unclear ownership for model-fallback behaviors.
- We have instrumentation but inconsistent signal aggregation for SLOs across hosted/dedicated/private.

Goal (90d):
1) Run 6 focused experiments that reduce median and P95 token-latency variance for critical APIs by >=10% in at least one workload profile.
2) Produce 3 decision-ready guardrails (feature flag, config knobs, or small service) that can be rolled into canary policy with monitoring and runbooks.
3) Define an SLO telemetry contract so experiment signal is comparable across environments.

Audience:
- Owners: SREs, Serving Runtime, Platform Engineers, Product-hosted-api PM
- Partners: Solutions Eng, Support, Dedicated customer engineers

Quick decision heuristic (one-pager):
- Success metrics: improvement in targeted signal (latency/cost/availability) + no >1 customer-facing regression in the experiment window.
- Safety gate: experiments touching traffic routing require automated rollback (circuit breaker) and a dry-run in staging with synthetic canaries.
- Graduation criteria (to policy):
  * Quantitative: stat-significant improvement (p<0.05) on primary metric across three independent runs or two customer segments.
  * Operational: <10% added alert volume and clear owner for oncall.
  * Observability: dashboards, traces, cost delta estimate, and test prompt set coverage.
- Rollback criteria: any measurable increase in P99 latency >15% for >30 minutes, or customer impact >SEV-2 for a production customer.

90-day experimentation playlist (prioritized):
1) Prefix cache eviction threshold tuning (serving-runtime)
   - Hypothesis: Increasing prefix cache retention for common prompts reduces KV load and lowers P95 latency for short convs by >12%.
   - Owner: Evan Brooks
   - Signals: cache hit rate, P50/P95 token latency, KV eviction churn, memory pressure
   - Risk & mitigation: memory blowup -> set OOM guard and staged knob ramp
   - Jira: JIRA-OBS-721

2) Batching window adaptive policy (platform-engineering + serving-runtime)
   - Hypothesis: Dynamically shortening batching window during tail events reduces P99 without big throughput loss.
   - Owner: Priya Desai
   - Signals: batch size distribution, latency by queue depth, throughput
   - Safety: feature flag + sampling 5% of traffic

3) Model-fallback circuit with quality gating (product-hosted-api)
   - Hypothesis: Smart fallback to quantized variant reduces tail latency while keeping hallucination rate within acceptable bounds for routable endpoints.
   - Owner: Lina Morales
   - Signals: fallback rate, user-facing error rate, eval prompt-set quality delta
   - Linked: confluence:CONFLUENCE-OPS-GUARD-PLANS-98

4) SLO telemetry contract pilot (observability + platform)
   - Hypothesis: A standardized SLO event format plus rollout reduces misalignment between hosted/dedicated SLO measurements and enables automated comparators.
   - Owner: Noah Kim
   - Signals: number of matching signals between infra metrics and SLO service, processing latency for SLO events
   - Deliverable: spec + example SDK integration for backend services

5) Autoscale warmup policy for dedicated pools (dedicated)
   - Hypothesis: Adding a warm-up window to scale-out reduces cold-start-induced tail latency on bursty workloads.
   - Owner: Sanjay Ramaswamy
   - Signals: pod ready time, request-queue latency, scale events per hour

6) Canary traffic shaping for multi-model routing (platform + product)
   - Hypothesis: Controlled routing weight changes reduce risk of capacity shocks and make rollouts smoother.
   - Owner: Cross-team (Evan + Priya)
   - Signals: routing mismatch errors, capacity headroom, application latency

Experiment cadence and guardrails:
- 2-week cadence per experiment: week 0 planning + env setup, week 1 gradual traffic ramp (1% -> 10% -> 25%), week 2 evaluation and decision window.
- All production ramps require: rollback toggle, synthetic canaries, owner on-call contact, and runbook stub checked into docs.
- Any experiment touching model quality must include a small prompt eval suite (10–30 prompts) and a quick manual review by Solutions Eng.

Roles & RACI (short):
- Responsible: experiment owner (runs the test, writes short postmortem)
- Accountable: eng-sre lead (signs graduation)
- Consulted: product-hosted-api PM, serving-runtime engineer, observability engineer
- Informed: support, dedicated-ops, security (if config touches network/auth)

Milestones & deliverables (per experiment):
- Plan doc + Jira ticket (day 0)
- Staging dry-run + canaries (day 3)
- 1% traffic ramp (day 5)
- 10% traffic ramp + monitoring (day 8)
- Decision window (day 10–14): pass/fail + postmortem + next action (graduate/iterate/rollback)

Template for experiment runbook (copyable):
- Title, hypothesis, owner, stakeholders
- Metrics (primary, secondary, safety)
- Staging checklist
- Rollout plan (percentage, timing, feature flag name)
- Observability links (dashboards, traces)
- Cost estimate
- Graduation checklist + signoff (names)

Open questions / unresolved:
- How aggressively do we want to standardize the SLO window across hosted vs dedicated? (tradeoff: signal comparability vs local customer tail behavior)
- Should cost delta be a hard abort criterion or advisory for now? (proposal: advisory for first quarter)
- Who owns the cross-customer quality baseline for fallback decisions? Product or Solutions Eng?

Next steps (this week):
- SRE lead to triage experiments into teams (owner confirmations) — action: @sre-leads on slack #ops-stability (due 2026-12-12)
- Observability to draft SLO telemetry contract prototype (noah) — due 2026-12-17
- Create three Jira tickets for top-priority experiments and add to sprint board (sanjay) — due 2026-12-15

Notes-to-self / meeting snippets:
- Quick sync with Lina and Priya 12/09: agree to block fallback canary behind manual gate until prompt-set is green.
- Evan suggests adding a small histogram of batch-window vs request-latency to the live dashboard (actioned).
